tasks.short: Maintain customer charge and payment records and resolve allocation exceptions.

steps.what: Check approved charge batches against supporting invoices in the {ERP}.
Enter validated charges into customer accounts in the {ERP}.
Download transactions from the {BANK}.
Match receipts to open invoices and record allocations in the {ERP}.
Investigate ambiguous receipts through the {EMAIL} and propose supported corrections.
Approve and record nonstandard ledger adjustments in the {ERP}.
Copy balances and unresolved items into a tracking workbook in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to import approved charges, receive transactions from the {BANK}, and allocate payments using exact references and approved matching rules. Keep ambiguous items in an {ERP} exception queue with supporting evidence, supervisor approval for nonstandard adjustments, and a live balance view that replaces the duplicate tracker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing import and matching features were incompletely configured. Inconsistent references and unclear exception ownership encouraged manual re-entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Established import formats and matching rules handle routine records. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation work without introducing a model into accounting decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Split payments, disputed invoices, duplicate receipts, and unexplained deductions need investigation. GDPR access and retention controls still apply; employee consultation depends on national rules and whether monitoring changes.
tasks.human_edge: Establish why money moved, distinguish a customer dispute from an allocation error, and support an adjustment with evidence.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of unresolved payment allocations by customer impact.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying transactions to resolving ambiguous receipts and preventing repeat errors. Posting and adjustment decision rights remain unchanged unless explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Explain whether a customer's payment has been received and allocated.
reach.learn: Read allocation states, distinguish receipt from settlement, and explain unresolved balances.

evidence.claim: Charge imports, exact payment matching, duplicate prevention, and exception queues are established deterministic patterns.
Exact documents order imports and stock synchronisation, supporting the integration pattern rather than proving payment reconciliation.
The step shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The company uses the {ERP} as the customer accounting record.
The baseline includes manual batch handling and a small duplicate tracker; companies with configured matching already have less work to remove.
Only unambiguous, balanced matches post automatically; all other receipts enter the exception queue.
The build configures existing posting controls and does not replace the accounting ledger.
unknowns: Which charge imports, bank feeds, and matching features are already enabled?
What proportion of receipts have reliable invoice references?
Who may approve adjustments, and which thresholds apply?
Are interfaces, test accounts, and representative transaction samples available?
Does the change trigger employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} configuration replace custom integration entirely?
Which matching rules achieve acceptable precision on historical transactions?
How will retries, reversals, duplicate imports, and partial payments be tested?
new_work: Resolve the exception queue and monitor its age.
Maintain matching rules and customer reference mappings.
Review failed imports, duplicate alerts, and reconciliation totals.
Maintain access permissions and adjustment audit trails.

tasks.short: Assemble credit evidence, calculate financial indicators, and prepare a reasoned credit assessment.

steps.what: Retrieve customer balances and payment history from the {ERP}.
Assemble investigation reports and financial documents from the {DOCS}.
Read reports in the {DOCS} and extract relevant facts with source references.

loop.input: Indexed reports and financial documents for one applicant.
loop.output: Candidate facts with source passages, dates, units, and unresolved contradictions.
loop.check: Validate schema, applicant identity, source location, dates, and numerical consistency; an analyst verifies material facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document, capped at 30 documents per case; unreadable or larger packs go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use direct mappings; variable narrative reports need bounded language extraction.

steps.what: Calculate ratios, exposure, and payment trends in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess repayment evidence, inconsistencies, and uncertainty against credit policy using the {DOCS}.
Write and approve a sourced assessment memo in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Analyst-authored conclusions, verified facts, calculated indicators, and an assessment template.
loop.output: A sourced memo expressing the analyst's conclusions and outstanding uncertainty.
loop.check: Check every figure against calculated data and every factual claim against evidence; the analyst approves the released memo.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at 2,000 words; unresolved discrepancies return the template to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle fixed sections, but case-specific explanations need bounded drafting from human conclusions.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins authorised history from the {ERP} to an indexed evidence pack in the {DOCS}, then calculates indicators with versioned formulas. Bounded loops extract sourced facts and draft the analyst's conclusions into a memo; the analyst verifies material evidence and approves the assessment before it reaches the credit decision maker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence arrives in different formats and periods. Document interpretation, calculations, and credit judgment are often mixed in one manual process.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can produce constrained, source-linked fields, while ordinary code performs calculations and consistency checks. This improves preparation without requiring automated credit judgment.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence may be stale, contradictory, or incomplete, and ratios do not settle repayment capacity. GDPR decision safeguards and EU AI Act classification require review of the actual use; human review must have substance rather than merely endorse an automated score.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh contradictory evidence, understand unusual financial circumstances, and defend a proportionate assessment.

ambition.what: Weekly evidence freshness decisions for open credit applications.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing explanations and requesting decisive evidence, with less time assembling packs and formatting memos. Credit approval limits remain unchanged.

reach.task: Triage application backlogs by missing evidence and review complexity.
reach.learn: Distinguish a documentation delay from a material credit concern without treating queue priority as a credit decision.

evidence.claim: Rossum documents extraction, rule checks, and exception routing for order documents; this is an adjacent pattern, not validation of credit assessment.
The SCHUFA judgment shows that a score strongly relied upon by a lender can itself constitute an automated decision.
Deterministic calculations with human credit judgment are a plausible design; the proposed savings and build ranges remain estimates.

assumptions: The task produces an assessment, while final credit authorisation is a separate action.
The baseline mixes business credit cases with some individual applicants; personal-data safeguards apply where relevant.
Models extract facts and express human conclusions; they do not generate credit scores or recommend acceptance.
Build ranges cover a limited deployment under existing credit policy, not a new regulated scoring service.
Documents are available electronically and may lawfully be processed for the stated purpose.
unknowns: Are applicants individuals, businesses, or both?
Which document types, languages, currencies, and reporting periods occur?
Who verifies facts, signs assessments, and makes final credit decisions?
Does the intended implementation fall within EU AI Act high-risk creditworthiness provisions?
Which GDPR safeguards and national credit rules apply to the actual process?
What additional compliance, procurement, or consultation lead time is required?
research_questions: Which documents already provide structured exports that remove the need for extraction?
Can source-linked extraction reliably detect period, currency, and applicant mismatches?
What evidence must an analyst see to challenge a draft assessment effectively?
Which representative cases expose material errors before rollout?
new_work: Verify extracted facts and resolve conflicting sources.
Maintain formulas, templates, and evidence freshness rules.
Evaluate extraction errors across document formats and applicant groups.
Maintain source lineage, access controls, and model processing arrangements.

tasks.short: Request external credit information and handle reciprocal reference disclosures.

steps.what: Verify applicant identity, enquiry purpose, and permission against the case in the {CRM}.
Request and retrieve reports through a credit bureau service in {OTHER}.
Contact bank references through the {TELEPHONY} to clarify missing or conflicting information.
File reports and reference notes against the applicant in the {DOCS}.
Prepare a reciprocal reference using permitted account facts and a template in the {DOCS}.
Approve recipient, permission, and disclosed facts before releasing the reply through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A controlled connector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} submits approved enquiries to the credit bureau service in {OTHER}, records receipts, and files results in the {DOCS} against the {CRM} case. A fixed-field generator prepares reciprocal references from permitted account facts, and the {WORKFLOW} releases them through the {EMAIL} only after recipient and disclosure approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate service logins, licensing restrictions, identity mismatches, and unclear disclosure permissions prevented reliable straight-through handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Where licensed interfaces exist, connectors and fixed-field templates remove rekeying and copying. No language model is needed for standard requests or replies.
tasks.still_hard: Access rights do not establish a lawful purpose for every enquiry or disclosure. GDPR, contractual restrictions, and national confidentiality rules still require case-specific checks; informal references may remain unavailable or disputed.
tasks.human_edge: Establish whether a request is legitimate, resolve identity ambiguity, and decide what information may fairly and lawfully be shared.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving disputed or missing reference information and less time moving reports between records. Disclosure authority remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Prepare factual reference replies and acknowledge correction requests.
reach.learn: Apply disclosure limits, verify recipients, and distinguish factual corrections from credit judgments.

evidence.claim: Licensed data retrieval, identity matching, request logging, and fixed-field replies can use deterministic integrations.
Rossum documents checked data transfer into business systems, supporting the integration pattern but not bureau access or reciprocal disclosure.
No digest source demonstrates this complete credit-reference workflow; feasibility, costs, and time estimates need local validation.

assumptions: The statement's 'potential creditors' means applicants or counterparties seeking credit; the intended population needs confirmation.
External credit information and reciprocal disclosures are distinct branches; shares represent a blended workload.
At least one external service offers a licensed interface or structured file exchange.
Reciprocal replies use approved factual fields, without free-text opinions or automatic disclosure.
The proposed correction-tracking service records progress and ownership; it does not alter external bureau data.
unknowns: Which external services are used, and what interface and redistribution rights are licensed?
What permits each enquiry and each reciprocal disclosure?
Which identifiers reliably distinguish applicants?
Which recipients, fields, and channels are approved for reference replies?
Who owns correction requests involving external providers?
What access, contracting, consultation, and retention requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing {CRM} or {WORKFLOW} connectors handle the licensed service?
How should ambiguous identity matches be stopped before an external enquiry?
Can a fixed-field reply meet normal requests without narrative drafting?
Which service restrictions prevent automated filing or reuse?
new_work: Maintain service credentials, entitlements, and connector mappings.
Review failed requests and ambiguous identity matches.
Maintain disclosure field lists and recipient verification procedures.
Handle applicant correction requests and preserve enquiry and disclosure logs.

tasks.short: Interview credit applicants to clarify financial circumstances and complete the credit evidence record.

steps.what: Review the application and prepare missing-data questions using the {DOCS}.
Arrange the interview through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Verify identity and explain the interview purpose over the {TELEPHONY}.
Discuss income, obligations, and unclear evidence with the applicant over the {TELEPHONY}.
Write and verify the financial interview record in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Typed interview notes, existing application fields, and the interview record template.
loop.output: A structured draft distinguishing applicant statements, documented facts, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link statements to notes, preserve uncertainty, validate numbers, and require interviewer approval before filing.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at 5,000 input words; unclear notes or unresolved facts return to manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Direct mappings handle form fields; variable typed explanations need bounded drafting into a consistent record.

steps.what: Send the applicant a missing-evidence checklist through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW} to build an interview agenda from missing application fields, arrange appointments through the {CALENDAR}, and send preparation checklists through the {EMAIL}. The clerk conducts the conversation, then a bounded drafting loop turns typed notes into a verified record in the {DOCS}; routine evidence requests use approved fields and templates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation and paperwork were treated as inseparable from the interview. Notes varied between interviewers, while scheduling and follow-up required separate manual actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, scheduling flows, and checklist rules are established capabilities. A small drafting loop can structure typed notes while keeping factual verification with the interviewer.
tasks.still_hard: Applicants may misunderstand questions, lack documents, or need sensitive explanations and accessible support. GDPR requires proportionate collection and controlled processing; recording or employee monitoring would add consultation questions under national rules, and creditworthiness automation would require EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, ask proportionate follow-up questions, recognise misunderstanding, and let applicants explain circumstances in their own words.
tasks.altitude: The clerk has more time for clarification and assisted completion, with less scheduling and note formatting. Authority over credit decisions does not change.

reach.task: Help an applicant understand evidence requirements before an interview.
reach.learn: Explain document requirements accessibly, protect financial information, and escalate questions requiring credit judgment.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, missing-field checklists, and template notifications can use existing workflow configuration.
Drafting structured records from typed notes is a bounded model use; credit-interview accuracy and savings are not demonstrated by the digest.
The NBER study found productivity gains for assisted support agents, providing adjacent evidence rather than a credit-interview outcome estimate.

assumptions: The telephone route is shown; in-person interviews retain the same preparation and recordkeeping changes.
The baseline uses typed notes and does not require call recording.
The preparation pack lets applicants review known fields and identify missing documents without requiring self-service completion.
Routine notifications contain approved requests and no credit acceptance, rejection, or new assessment.
Conversation time falls only modestly because clarification remains central.
unknowns: How many interviews occur by telephone, in person, or with accessibility support?
Which questions and identity checks are mandatory?
Are applications structured enough to generate a reliable missing-data agenda?
Can typed notes be processed in the permitted environment?
Who approves interview records and handles disputed statements?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Which questions can disappear because reliable answers already exist in the application?
Can applicants use the preparation pack without digital access or specialist financial knowledge?
Does drafting preserve qualifications and distinguish applicant statements from verified evidence?
Do interviewers detect omissions during realistic record-review exercises?
new_work: Review draft interview records and correct unsupported statements.
Maintain question lists, accessible preparation materials, and evidence templates.
Handle scheduling exceptions and applicants needing assisted completion.
Monitor drafting quality, processing permissions, and record retention.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward evidence quality, allocation exceptions, careful applicant conversations, and defensible credit analysis. Credit decisions and sensitive disclosures retain explicit human authority; automation alone grants no additional decision rights.
reach: Customer service representatives: explain payment status and application evidence requirements.
Correspondence clerks: prepare controlled factual references and correction acknowledgements.
First-line administrative supervisors: triage evidence bottlenecks and coordinate exception handling.
skills_to_grow: Configure matching rules, forms, templates, and exception queues.
Read financial indicators and trace them to source evidence.
Review extracted facts and drafted records without rubber-stamping.
Apply GDPR safeguards, disclosure permissions, and relevant national rules.
Conduct accessible interviews and explain uncertainty clearly.
Monitor integration failures and maintain auditable records.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an applicant evidence service that combines preparation checklists, correction tracking, and clear explanations of missing information. Credit analysts retain assessment authority, while clerks gain a defined coordination role across applicants, finance, and external reference providers.
